edges.mechanism: Taurine lowers BP (about -4 mmHg SBP, -1.4 to -2.5 mmHg DBP in MAs) via H2S and TRPC3-mediated vascular calcium-influx inhibition; additive lowering with antihypertensives is plausible.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs (20 and 34 RCTs) plus RCTs in prehypertension and T2D; no direct drug-interaction study.

edges.mechanism: Taurine modestly lowers FBG, HbA1c and HOMA-IR; it improved metformin plus DPP4-inhibitor therapy in a diabetic mouse model; additive glucose lowering is possible.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs (low certainty) plus mouse data; no human combination PK or outcome study.

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose and insulin-resistance lowering (FBG -5.9 mg/dL, HbA1c -0.21%).
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs including T2D trials at 3 g/d; low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Vigabatrin lowers plasma taurine (67% in animals; low or undetectable in 5 of 6 infants) and taurine deficiency drives its retinal phototoxicity; taurine supplementation was protective in rodents.
edges.evidence: Animal study plus infant plasma data; case reports of partial ERG reversal in SSADH deficiency.

edges.mechanism: Taurine is a GABA-A and glycine-receptor agonist; drowsiness and ataxia occurred in children taking taurine with anticonvulsants.
edges.evidence: Uncontrolled pediatric case series (n=25) plus receptor pharmacology.

edges.mechanism: Adjunctive taurine 4 g/d improved BPRS total and psychotic subscale scores in first-episode psychosis on low-dose antipsychotics; no cognitive effect.
edges.evidence: Single phase 2 RCT (n=121, 86 analysed).

edges.mechanism: Taurine inhibits platelet activation and aggregation; additive antiplatelet effect is theoretical.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of animal and human platelet studies; no clinical bleeding data.

edges.mechanism: Taurine 1 g/d added to iron sulfate gave additional Hb, RBC and ferritin gains in iron-deficiency anaemia.
edges.evidence: Double-blind RCT, n=51 women.

edges.mechanism: Co-ingested in energy drinks. A high-volume energy drink raised SBP and QTc (driven by caffeine, not taurine); taurine was pro-arrhythmic in an isolated rabbit heart; caffeine plus taurine raised MAP in humans; combined ergogenic effect on anaerobic capacity and reaction time.
edges.evidence: RCT crossover (n=38), small human trials, network MA, ex vivo animal model; review suggests taurine may blunt caffeine effects.

edges.mechanism: Beta-alanine competes with taurine at the transporter TauT (SLC6A6) and lowers muscle taurine in mice; in humans 6.4 g/d for 24 weeks did not change muscle taurine.
edges.evidence: In vitro, cryo-EM and mouse data; human RCT and MA show no muscle-taurine depletion.

edges.mechanism: Taurine plus creatine improved time to exhaustion in heat vs placebo; no added repeated-sprint benefit.
edges.evidence: Small single-blind crossover RCT (n=12).

edges.mechanism: Taurine (3 g/d) and magnesium (340 mg/d) each improved endothelial progenitor cell function and lowered oxidative stress; combined effect in hypertensive rats.
edges.evidence: Small human study in healthy men plus rat data.

edges.mechanism: NAC plus taurine as dual antioxidant in CKD; retrospective data show lower uACR and serum creatinine vs standard care.
edges.evidence: Open-label RCT (n=69) and retrospective comparative study (n=450); low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Taurine raised astrocyte glutathione only with adequate B9; a taurine plus B6/B9/B12 blend improved effortful motivation.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCT (n=44) plus in vitro data.

edges.mechanism: Taurine/diltiazem/vitamin E formula slowed visual-field loss in retinitis pigmentosa.
edges.evidence: Double-blind controlled study (n=62); combination, so taurine's own effect cannot be separated.

edges.mechanism: Both taurine and glycine activate glycine receptors; additive inhibitory neurotransmission is theoretical.
edges.evidence: Receptor pharmacology only.

edges.mechanism: The kidney regulates taurine pool size and excretion; safety evidence is strong only up to 3 g/d in healthy adults and dosing in advanced CKD is unstudied.
edges.evidence: Reviews and OSL risk assessment; no CKD dose-safety trials.

edges.mechanism: Taurine restores taurine modification of mitochondrial tRNA-Leu(UUR); 9-12 g/d reduced stroke-like episode relapse rate (2.22 to 0.72/yr). A 2026 consensus judged efficacy unproven.
edges.evidence: Open-label phase III (n=10), case reports, consensus statement.

edges.mechanism: 2 g/d reduced muscle cramp frequency and severity; 1 g/d did not improve fatigue overall; mild AEs in 11.8%.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCT (n=30), open-label RCT (n=220), SR of RCTs.

edges.mechanism: Adjunctive taurine may improve NYHA class and LVEF; additive effects with HF drugs on BP and heart rate are possible.
edges.evidence: MA subgroup and SR of mostly low-quality studies; small crossover RCT; one HF RCT retracted.

edges.mechanism: Supplementation raises plasma taurine (Cmax about 1.5 h, t1/2 about 1 h), which confounds use of taurine as an aging biomarker; levels vary with timing of the last dose.
edges.evidence: Human PK study and RCTs; biomarker validity disputed in human cohorts.

edges.mechanism: Loss of TauT transport causes early-onset retinal dystrophy with low plasma taurine; patients may be candidates for investigational oral taurine.
edges.evidence: Multicenter case series (7 affected, 4 families) with functional assays.
